about: Trent'uno («Trent'uno»), pp. 45-46 of the Turin rulebook «Primi elementi e regole del giuoco de' tarocchi» (Torino, Soffietti, 1787): Sedici with eight covered cards to each player and thirty-one points to win (pp. 45-46: «Premesse tutte le sopradette regole»). Everything of Sedici applies unless said otherwise: the Fool is the lowest trionfo and counts one point, Bagatto takes it, the cards are counted singly, the dealer goes on dealing until somebody says «fuora» (pp. 36-41, 51). The section does not say how many play; it is read after Sedici, for two, three or four. A plain card is worth 1 (since revision 2, by calculation; Dummett 1980, p. 269, allows it), a false claim is paid double under 16 points, and when the pack runs out before anybody has said «fuora» the hand ends with no payment: our decisions, each leaf says whose reading. A match is a race to five points, each game won being one: Prammatica [1846], pp. 11-12 says it of Sedici, and Trent'uno «non differisce dal Sedici che nel numero»; the number five is our reading of p. 13. Marks: [D] documented, [R] our reading, [S] sources silent.

torino1846.cite: L. B., Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, part I (Grammatica del giuocatore), Torino, Serra, [1846]

dummett1980.cite: M. Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London, Duckworth, 1980; chapter XIII, pp. 258-279 (partial scan held, p. 268 missing)

prammatica1846.cite: L. B., Prammatica del giuocatore di tarocchi ossia regole indispensabili per gli amatori di simile passatempo, Torino, Serra, [1846] (separate issue, cover dated 1846, deposited 27 December 1845; reprinted from the same setting, same pages, as part II of Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, Torino, Serra, [1846])

count.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 28 (three players «come usasi anche a Trent'uno al più»), p. 31 (Trent'uno al meno: «si giuoca in due, come in più persone»); four players our reading. Torino 1787, p. 45: «Premesse tutte le sopradette … del Sedici, rimane … a giuocare al Trent'uno»; the number of players is not stated and is read as that of Sedici, two (p. 15), three (p. 43), four (p. 36).

direction.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35, 37: «gli altri sempre a destra procedendo»: play passes to the right.

first_dealer.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 16: cards are turned up for each side, «se viene prima da questa parte un Trionfo, mischierò io»: the side that first receives a trionfo shuffles and deals first.

cut_by.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 16-17: the player on the dealer's left cuts («di dar a coppare a chi ti siede a sinistra»); if he declines the next on the left, if all decline the dealer deals as the pack lies.

cut_min.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 16: «Una carta sola non si può coppare»: the page forbids only a cut of one card; that each part keeps at least two cards is our reading.

dealer_rotation.source: [R] For two: Trent'uno is played by the rules of Sedici (Torino 1787, p. 45: «Premesse tutte le sopradette regole»), and there p. 42 (rule 44): «colui, cui tocca a mischiar le carte, è quegli per avventura, che abbia guadagnato»: the next dealer may be the winner; p. 70: «tocca al compagno appresso a mischiare»: the deal alternates. Revision 9 (answer 2 of the lead session) sets aside revision 8 B4. [R] For three and four: the deal goes round to the right whoever won, as in Sedici for three and four: p. 19 (rule 6), «lascierai correr la mano al tuo compagno a destra», and p. 42 (rule 44). Other reading: for two, the winner hands the whole pack to his companion (p. 41), so the loser deals.

mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 40, 45: «Premesse tutte le sopradette regole»: carried over from Sedici, where each player makes his own points (p. 40: «Quando adunque tu prima del tuo compagno sappi d'aver fatti sedici punti»); the first to thirty-one says «fuora».

deck.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 9-10: «Settant'otto Tarocchi si richiedono»: twenty-two trionfi (the Fool is n. 0 among them) and fourteen cards in each of the four suits.

trump_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13, 37-39, 46: as at Sedici, the Angel XX takes the World XXI and none takes the Angel, the Fool is the lowest and «Bagatto piglia il Folle» (p. 46). The list is highest first.

suit_order.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 11-13: in swords and batons the larger number takes the smaller; in cups and coins «la carta di numero inferiore prende quella di numero superiore, eccetto le figure» (the ace takes the two up to the ten); the courts stand above every numeral. The order among the courts is printed, pp. 11-12: «il Re bensì prende la Donna, il Cavallo, il Fante».

card_points.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14, 38: king 5, queen 4, knight 3, jack 2, the Angel 5, Bagatto 5, and «il Folle al Sedici, ed al Trent'uno conta un sol punto» (p. 38); a plain card is worth count.plain_value.

fool.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 36, 38, 46: at Trent'uno as at Sedici the Fool takes as a trionfo and a lone Fool must be played; Bagatto takes it («Bagatto piglia il Folle»), it takes no Bagatto (p. 38).

options.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 21 (rule 10): «quanto si giuochi la partita semplice, qualunque sia il giuoco, che facciasi»: the stake of the simple game is settled before the deal. The book names no amount (p. 15 plays «un quattrino per ciascuna partita» as an example); the list of choices is the table's.

phases.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 39, 45: «Premesse tutte le sopradette regole»: the dealer goes on dealing eight cards to each until someone says «fuora» (the repeat is the rule of Sedici, p. 39, not repeated for Trent'uno).

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 45-46: «al giuoco Trent'uno si danno otto carte coperte (s'intende sempre)».

packets.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 18, 41-42, 45: the ways of dealing are printed for four cards; «Premesse tutte le sopradette regole» carries the choice and the announcement over.

packets_announced.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 17-18, 42, 45: the dealer says before the cut how he will deal; carried over from Sedici.

dead.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 39, 45: carried over from Sedici, the cards of the earlier rounds stay out of the pack until the game is won. Dummett 1980, p. 269 reads Sedici so: «without returning to the pack the cards already played».

first_leader.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 37 (general rule): «Colui, che or ultimo ha preso la mano ... deve essere il primo a giuocare»: each later round of the same game, after a new deal, is led by the taker of the last trick; the book does not say it for the rounds (p. 39); Dummett is silent. The first round of every game is led by the player on the dealer's right, [D] p. 35: «Chi è a destra di chi dà, comincia». Trent'uno follows the rules of Sedici (p. 45). Other readings: the player on the dealer's right leads every round (stood until revision 8); the last taker of the game before leads (previous_last_taker).

next_leader.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 37: «Colui, che or ultimo ha preso la mano ... deve essere il primo a giuocare»; «Facciamo un altro esempio al Trent'uno, od al Sedici medesimo» (p. 36).

follow_suit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 35-36, 45: the answer in the suit asked, as at Sedici.

must_trump.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 36 prints the duty for Partita and the games after it: «si risponderà e prenderà con un Trionfo»; carried back to this game. Torino 1787, pp. 36-37, in an example «al Trent'uno, od al Sedici», plays so: «io Spade non ne tengo, metto sul tuo sette un Trionfo». Torino 1787, p. 49 (Baronetti) prints the same duty: «se non ho carte della medesima sequenza prendo con Trionfi».

must_overtrump.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 36-37: the book states no duty to beat the trionfo on the table.

phases.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 45-46: «con trent'un punto la partita è guadagnata»; «chiamarti prontamente fuora innanzi agli altri compagni, quando lo sii senza fallo».

target.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 46: «con trent'un punto la partita è guadagnata».

claim_when.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 40: «Quando adunque tu prima del tuo compagno sappi d'aver fatti sedici punti»: «fuora» is said as soon as one knows the points are made (said of Sedici; Trent'uno «Premesse tutte le sopradette regole», p. 45); Dummett 1980, p. 269: the first to say it wins. The table lets a player say it on any turn of his own, also in the middle of a trick (own_turn). Other readings: only right after a trick, by its taker (after_trick, stood until revision 8); at any moment, also out of turn (any_time).

after_first_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 40-41, 45: for two, as at Sedici, the game is won when a player is out. [R] For three and four the same is read: rules 45 and 47 (pp. 43-45) have a second winner only when the others play on («a scaricare»), which is not carried over here.

false_claim.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 45-46 and Torino [1846], part I, pp. 29-30 print no line; ours: half of 31, as Sedici's eight of sixteen (p. 39). To whom it is paid is not said; paid to each other player, ours: Dummett 1980, p. 269 says so of Sedici («he pays 1 game point to each of the other players»), and Trentuno «is said to be played exactly like Sedici»; he does not say it of Trentuno itself. Other reading: in the Savoy «À Fora» (rules of Annecy, in Depaulis 1984) a false claim loses the game and no more, at 30 points too. [R] In a race (match.kind) a double row gives each other player two points, a «vada doppio», and a simple row one: Prammatica [1846], p. 13 prints the «vada doppio» for a revoke at Trent'uno al meno; carried over to the false claim, ours.

after_false_claim.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 20 (rule 9): «ma seguirassi questa sull'istesso piede»: a mistake is paid and the same game goes on; read for a false «fuora». p. 39 (rule 41) prints only the payment. Other version: a false claim loses the game, as in the Savoy «À Fora» (rules of Annecy, in Depaulis 1984).

replace.what: a false «fuora»: does the game go on or end

stock_empty.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 39 and Torino [1846], part I, p. 26: «finchè alcuno si chiami fuora»; an empty pack is not mentioned. Ours after Dummett 1980, p. 269, who names two guesses: the hand is given up without payment, or all the cards are dealt again; the first is played. Revision 1 gathered the untaken cards and dealt on, which cannot be done: too few cards are left for another round.

replace.what: the pack runs out and nobody has said «fuora»

group.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 51-52: «E non basta per contare (come al Sedici, ed al Trent'uno) una carta sola»: at Sedici and Trent'uno the cards are counted one at a time («per volta», p. 52).

trick_multipliers.source: [R] Torino 1787: the count is the one the section names; the book prints no trick multiplier and no war in these games (x2 and x4 are Duello's own).

last_trick_bonus.source: [R] Torino 1787: the book prints no bonus for the last trick (the +5 is Duello's own).

plain_value.source: [S] Torino 1787, pp. 13-14, 51 and Torino [1846], part I, p. 30 give no value to a plain card counted singly; ours: 1. Dummett 1980, p. 269 counts it 0, adds that 1 is possible and that with 0 it is «quite common for no one to reach 31 points». The Savoy twin of the game, «À Fora» (rules of Annecy, in Depaulis 1984), counts plain cards and the Fool 1. A rough model (revision 2): with 0 the pack runs out before anyone has 31 in 29 % of games for two, 58 % for three, 87 % for four; with 1 in 0 %, 0 %, 5 %.

replace.what: the value of a plain card counted singly

winner.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 46: «con trent'un punto la partita è guadagnata»: the first to be out wins.

game_points.source: [D] Prammatica [1846], pp. 11-12: at Sedici a match seldom ends «nel primo punto che si vince o si perde», each game won or lost being a point, a «vada»; Trent'uno «non differisce dal Sedici che nel numero di trentuno» (p. 12). So a game won gives its winner one point in the race of match.kind. The stake of Torino 1787, p. 41 is still paid by the settle phase.

unit.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 21, 41, 45: «sarai pagato secondo fu convenuta la partita»; «Premesse tutte le sopradette regole».

mode.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 41, 43, 45: as at Sedici each loser pays the winner (for two players the one loser); the variant «a scaricare» of p. 43 is not carried over here. The number of players is itself our reading.

amount.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 21, 41: the agreed simple game.

kind.source: [D] Prammatica [1846], pp. 11-12: at Sedici «Se poi a più punti si stabilisce la partita o la presa», and Trent'uno «non differisce dal Sedici che nel numero di trentuno»: the match is played to several points, each game won being one. The book of 1787 describes one game only. Other version, also printed (pp. 11, 13): the match «al primo vada», every game stands alone and is paid at once; then the length of a match is ours, one round of dealers (match.kind ledger with match.dealer_rounds 1).

target.source: [R] Prammatica [1846], p. 13 names the match played «a più punti non meno di cinque» in the article on Trent'uno al meno, which refers back to Sedici and Trent'uno; the page names no other number. Ours: five, the least the page allows. [S] When the leaders are level at five or more, another game is played, until one leads alone: the sources say nothing of it; other version, the match is drawn. Which custom was played, the race or «al primo vada», is open (match.kind).

replace.what: which custom was played, a race or «al primo vada», to how many points, and what is done when the leaders are level

effect.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 33-34, 38, 45: as at Sedici a player who does not answer in the suit asked pays the simple game to all (rule 35). In a race (match.kind) Prammatica [1846] reads otherwise: the offender loses a point, p. 12, of Trent'uno al più: «Chi rinnega, strettamente parlando, perde il Vada»; p. 11: «perdono il punto, così detto Vada semplice».
[D] Torino 1787, p. 42 (rule 43) and p. 45: a dealer who changes his method without timely notice pays the simple game to all.

[D] Torino 1787, pp. 18-19, 45 (rules 5 and 6, general rules kept by «Premesse tutte le sopradette regole»): «Pagherai similmente la partita, se darai giuoco … carta di più, o di meno»; if the fault is found at the end the dealer «pagherai d'obbligazione tutti i giuocatori» and «lascierai correr la mano al tuo compagno a destra»: he pays every other player and the deal passes to the right. [R] The redeal (hand: redeal) is our reading: the book prints the payment, not a new deal of the same hand.

variants.source: [D] Prammatica [1846], p. 12 (Trent'uno al più): «Il Matto … vale come semplice Tarocco: egli prende Bagatto occorrendo»: the Fool is an ordinary trionfo and takes Bagatto. Against it Torino 1787, p. 46: «Bagatto piglia il Folle», and Torino [1846], part I, p. 29: «Bagatto, salvo qualche luogo ove praticasi viceversa, piglia il Folle». By Prammatica [1846], p. 12 the winner is the first to have made the points, not the first to say so; the engine does not play that.

trump_order.source: [R] Prammatica [1846], p. 12: «egli prende Bagatto occorrendo»: the Fool takes Bagatto. The page does not place it among the other trionfi; read as just above Bagatto and below the II, every other trionfo takes it. The list is highest first.

play.value: lead kings seldom, hoping to take other players' queens, knights or jacks with them
play.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 46: «i Re si giuocan di rado sulla … o i Cavalli, od i Fanti»: advice of the book; it never binds a human player.

play.value: if you can hope to catch the Bagatto and hold many trionfi, lead trionfi, the more so with a king or a queen to save
play.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 46: «Se v'ha speranza di … tanto più, se … o Donna a salvarti».

play.value: keep in mind the cards already on the table and say «fuora» promptly when sure
play.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 46: «Conviene aver mente alle carte già venute giù in tavola»; «chiamarti prontamente fuora innanzi agli altri compagni, quando lo sii senza fallo».

left_out.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, p. 30: «passar o gettar via carte», replaced from the pack, by general consent.
left_out.why: A custom by agreement, not in Torino 1787; not played.
